summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman was admitted with severe bilateral lower extremity swelling, a 18-pound weight gain, and erythema on the left shin concerning for cellulitis. She was started on IV vancomycin for a 7-day course, with improvement in redness and leukocytosis. Diuresis was attempted with IV furosemide and a lasix drip, resulting in initial fluid loss but complicated by acute kidney injury (creatinine rising to 1.6) and hypokalemia with contraction alkalosis. Diuresis was discontinued, and she was transitioned back to home oral diuretics. Echocardiogram showed normal heart function, and lower extremity ultrasound ruled out deep vein thrombosis. Her swelling improved with conservative measures including ACE wraps. She was discharged home with home health services, instructions to monitor weight, and follow-up for lab monitoring and lymphedema evaluation.
problems: Cellulitis and abscess of leg, except foot
Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
